bullets.text: Oman reported positive talks regarding a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, though a clear breakthrough has not yet been announced.
The US has offered $1 billion in security aid to Colombia as its new right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, took office, vowing an "all-out war" on "narco-terrorism."
Spain will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy, responding to similar measures by Rome following a large influx of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta.
The number of fur seals on Deen Maar Island, once Australia's largest colony, has significantly declined due to pollution affecting pups.
Centrelink is pursuing debts over 40 years old, despite previous agreements to waive old arrears, raising concerns from advocates about accuracy.
Experts are raising 'alarm bells' over the hospitality recruitment app Supp, which classifies gig-workers as contractors and requires ABNs, potentially denying them casual work entitlements.
Berkshire Hathaway's chief, Greg Abel, has ended a three-year selling streak by investing a net $20 billion into stocks, putting Warren Buffett's cash pile to work.
Highly-indebted companies are increasingly shifting from private credit loans to cheaper bank loan markets, driven by the current environment of higher-for-longer interest rates.
African countries are increasingly moving away from the US dollar, with the yuan and local currencies poised to benefit from this shift.
